title: Start Finishing: How to Go from Idea to Done
description: Awards for Start Finishing : • Publishers Weekly Fall 2019 Top 10 Business and Economics Books • Book Authority Best New Book in (the categories of) Time Management, Success, Productivity, and Goal Setting • Kirkus Reviews Top Indie Book • Montaigne Medal Finalist • Independent Publisher Book Award 2020: Silver Award for Business/Careers/Sales • Eric Hoffer Book Award 2020: Grand Prize Productivity Meets Purpose—Discover a Powerful Nine-Step Method to Start Finishing the Work That Matters Most How much of your time and attention lately has been focused on things that truly matter to you? Most people's honest answer is: not enough. Everyone is buried by busywork, responsibility, distraction, and fatigue. The joy-producing, difference-making ideas are waiting for when the time is right, when the current project is over, when they have a little more money, when the kids are grown, or when they get a more understanding boss. They are waiting for someday . The trouble is someday never comes on its own. Start Finishing presents a nine-step method for converting an idea into a project by addressing the challenges you'll face and getting the project on a reality-based schedule. title: THE UNSCATTERED MIND: HOW TO STOP DOING EVERYTHING AND FINALLY FINISH SOMETHING
description: Are you tired of watching your potential leak through a hundred tiny structural holes? Most mornings, you wake up with a chest full of ambition and a clear mental map of what you want to achieve. But by the time the sun goes down, you are left with nothing but a vague, heavy sense of exhaustion. You look back at your day and realize you spent ten hours frantically jumping between open browser tabs, managing minor emergencies, scrolling through feeds, and starting three different tasks without ever crossing a single finish line. You are working constantly, yet you are completely stuck. In The Unscattered Mind , you will discover a clinical, zero-fluff playbook designed to help you strip away the noise, outsmart your own biology, and build a fortress around your attention. This book does not exist to turn you into a cold productivity machine—it exists to help you rescue your mind from a permanent state of fragmentation. Inside this premium strategic guide, you will learn to: Audit Your Chaos: Face the harsh biological reality of dopamine loops and why your brain actively betrays your long-term intentions. Destroy the Multitasking Illusion: Master the rare art of deep, single-tasking execution and eliminate the cognitive switching residue that drains your daily fuel. Escape the Comparison Trap: Stop looking sideways at everyone else's curated highlight reels and build your own internal scoreboard for exponential growth. Isolate Your Lead Domino: Apply a brutal filter to contract your vision, say a definitive "no" to the trivial, and weaponize your highest-caliber energy. Build a Unerring Focus System: Establish dedicated sanctuaries, rigid 90-minute time windows, and startup rituals that turn focus into a reflex. title: Stop Procrastinating and Start Finishing: A Simple Step-by-Step Guide to Beating Avoidance
description: Procrastination can make even simple tasks feel heavy. If you keep delaying important responsibilities, starting projects but not finishing them, waiting for motivation, or feeling overwhelmed by everything you need to do, you are not alone. Stop Procrastinating and Start Finishing is a beginner-friendly self-help guide for anyone who wants to stop avoiding, start taking action, and build the confidence to finish what matters without relying on pressure, guilt, or perfection. Inside, you’ll learn how to: Understand why procrastination really happens Make starting feel easier and less overwhelming Break big tasks into finishable steps Reduce distractions and mental resistance Build follow-through with realistic routines Recover after missed days without quitting Create a simple finish-friendly routine Follow a practical 30-day start and finish plan With clear guidance, reflection prompts, simple exercises, and realistic strategies, this book helps readers move from stuck and overwhelmed to steady, focused, and capable of completing more of what matters. title: The Less You Do, the More You Get Done: A Practical System to Stop Feeling Overwhelmed, Fo
description: Most people don't have a time problem. They have an attention problem. Every day begins with good intentions. You plan to work on an important project, learn a new skill, or finally make progress on something that could change your future. Then the messages arrive. Emails pile up. Meetings appear. Notifications interrupt your thoughts. Before you realize it, the day is over, and the work that mattered most is still waiting. If this feels familiar, you're not alone. This book isn't another collection of productivity hacks that promise to help you squeeze more tasks into every hour. It's a practical guide to helping you spend your limited time, attention, and energy on work that actually creates meaningful progress. Instead of relying on complicated systems or expensive apps, you'll learn a simple framework that can fit into real life. You'll discover how to decide what deserves your attention before the day makes that decision for you, how to turn overwhelming projects into clear next actions, and how to protect your focus in a world designed to steal it. You'll also learn why being busy often creates the illusion of progress, how constant task switching quietly drains your productivity, when to schedule demanding work for your highest-energy hours, and why removing unnecessary commitments can be more powerful than working faster. Throughout the book, each chapter builds on the same practical system, helping you create habits that are easy to repeat rather than routines that collapse after a few days. You'll find simple exercises that can be applied immediately, whether you have ten minutes before work, an afternoon to reset your schedule, or a week to build a more sustainable way of working.
